flagged.evidence: The title says “An oblique plane wave requires a longitudinal electric component,” but the Example only constructs q=(κ,0) with e_perp=(E0,0) and concludes that e_z cannot be zero while keeping that amplitude. The in-scope theorem gives e_z=−(q·e_perp)/k_z for an exact mode. For the same oblique q, choose e=(0,E0,0) and b=(−k_zE0/ω,0,κE0/ω), where k_z²+κ²=k_0². Then K·e=K·b=0, K×e=ωb, and K×b=−ωe/c², so this is an exact source-free Maxwell plane wave with e_z=0. The generic title therefore overstates what the example proves; the longitudinal component is required for its chosen transverse polarization.
